title: Dependency-scoped loop transaction effect envelope
claim_boundary: Not live FRANK evidence and not proof of production ClayCode runtime safety. Tests three commit policies in an explicit constructed state/capability transition model.

policies.naive: Permit observed at decision time is retained across recurrent attempts without state/capability freshness revalidation.
policies.global_epoch_guard: Commit only if target state, unrelated state and capability epoch all remain unchanged and capability remains allowed.
policies.dependency_envelope: Commit only if exact decision target read-set remains unchanged and capability epoch/current validity remain unchanged; unrelated state churn does not invalidate.

result: In this constructed model, stale permit reuse is unsafe; whole-state epoch validation is safe but rejects unrelated-state churn; exact read-set plus capability-epoch validation achieved zero unsafe commits and zero false aborts across the enumerated and fuzzed cases.
candidate_invariant: Effect commit binds exact decision read-set identity plus current capability epoch/validity; unrelated state changes do not invalidate the effect.
counterhypothesis_not_resolved: A single-threaded serialized H1 runtime or whole-ledger CAS may be operationally cheap enough that dependency-scoped validation is unnecessary on the real Ubuntu target.
next_test: Replay frozen H1 effect-bearing episodes under whole-ledger CAS vs per-domain/object dependency envelopes; inject unrelated churn, revoke/regrant, queue delay, crash/restart and child-code effects; compare safety, false aborts, latency and recovery.
